english: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a function that is continuous at $x=0$, with $f(0)=-1$ and $f(x)-f\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)=\dfrac{3x^{2}}{4}$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $g(x)=\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\Big(1+|f(x)|^{n}\Big)^{1/n}$. Then the product of all real numbers at which $g$ is not differentiable is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ एक फलन है जो $x=0$ पर सतत है, $f(0)=-1$ है तथा सभी $x\in\mathbb{R}$ के लिए $f(x)-f\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)=\dfrac{3x^{2}}{4}$ है। माना कि $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\Big(1+|f(x)|^{n}\Big)^{1/n}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। तब उन सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं का गुणनफल, जिन पर $g$ अवकलनीय नहीं है, ______ है।
solution: $|x^{2}-1|>1\iff|x|>\sqrt2$ (note $|x^{2}-1|=1$ also at $x=0$, but there $|x^{2}-1|\le1$ on both sides, so $g=1$ near $0$)
$g=1$ on $[-\sqrt2,\sqrt2]$, $g=x^{2}-1$ outside: slopes $0$ and $\pm2\sqrt2$ at $\pm\sqrt2$; non-differentiable only at $\pm\sqrt2$
solution_full: Finding $f$. Applying the relation at $\dfrac{x}{2^{k}}$: $f\left(\dfrac{x}{2^{k}}\right)-f\left(\dfrac{x}{2^{k+1}}\right)=\dfrac{3x^{2}}{4\cdot4^{k}}$. Adding for $k=0,1,\dots,m-1$ telescopes to $f(x)-f\left(\dfrac{x}{2^{m}}\right)=\dfrac{3x^{2}}{4}\cdot\dfrac{1-4^{-m}}{1-\frac14}=x^{2}\left(1-4^{-m}\right)$.

As $m\to\infty$, $\dfrac{x}{2^{m}}\to0$ and, because $f$ is continuous at $0$, $f\left(\dfrac{x}{2^{m}}\right)\to f(0)=-1$. Hence $f(x)=x^{2}-1$ for every $x$. (Without continuity at $0$ the relation alone would not determine $f$.)
$|x^{2}-1|>1$ means $x^{2}>2$ (the other case $x^{2}<0$ is impossible). So $g(x)=x^{2}-1$ for $|x|>\sqrt2$ and $g(x)=1$ for $|x|\le\sqrt2$.

At $x=\pm\sqrt2$, $g$ is continuous (value $1$) but the one-sided derivatives are $0$ and $2x=\pm2\sqrt2$, so $g$ is not differentiable there. At $x=0$, $|f(0)|=1$, but $|x^{2}-1|=1-x^{2}\le1$ nearby, so $g\equiv1$ near $0$ and is differentiable. Elsewhere $g$ is a polynomial or constant.
Points of non-differentiability: $\sqrt2$ and $-\sqrt2$; their product is $-2$.
originality_note: New: a halving functional equation determines f only through continuity at 0 (telescoping to the limit), and f then feeds an n-th root limit that produces max{1, |f|}, whose corners must be separated from the false candidate x = 0 where |f| = 1 tangentially (way 2). Closest known: Cauchy-type equations f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y) with continuity, and lim (a^n + b^n)^{1/n} = max(a, b). Different because: the two ideas feed each other and the touching point x = 0 is a deliberate trap.
blueprint_concepts: Functions defined by a limit, e.g. lim of f(x)^n as n -> infinity
Continuity of a function defined by a functional equation

concept_use.Functions defined by a limit, e.g. lim o: g(x) = lim (1 + |f(x)|^n)^{1/n} = max{1, |x^2 - 1|} is obtained from the n-limit.
concept_use.Continuity of a function defined by a fu: The relation f(x) - f(x/2) = 3x^2/4 telescopes, and continuity at 0 gives f(x/2^m) -> f(0), hence f(x) = x^2 - 1.
